EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows strong C–H stretches at 2946 cm⁻¹ and 3014 cm⁻¹, indicating both aliphatic (∼2950 cm⁻¹) and vinylic/hetero-substituted (∼3000–3020 cm⁻¹) C–H bonds; this is consistent with the unsaturated heteroaromatic ring and methyl group in CC1NS1, but less so for the fully saturated halogenated alkanes (2, 10) or P-Cl compounds (4, 9). The dominant Raman band at 525 cm⁻¹ matches a strong C–S skeletal stretch often observed in thiazole/thiazoline rings, while the 716 cm⁻¹ band corresponds to C–S/N–S ring modes. The 1071 cm⁻¹ peak fits C–N/C–S ring stretching. The 1450 cm⁻¹ band is attributable to CH₃ bending, expected for the terminal methyl group in CC1NS1. Overall, the pattern of sulfur- and nitrogen-containing ring vibrations plus mixed aliphatic/unsaturated C–H features aligns best with the thiazoline-type molecule CC1NS1.
